title: Review of c02's chemoton at 1.5x resolution: replicates on fresh seed 8 (a catalyst-ringed double vesicle persists to t=600, K rim/core 6.97; a catalyst-free vesicle persists beside it)
summary: Ran world_res15.py (288^2 at the same physical size, dt 0.005) unchanged on seed 8 to t=600. From noise, micelles and pearled strands form by t~24-51; one body captures the catalyst and closes into a double-walled vesicle with K beaded on its bilayer by t~132, which persists unchanged to t=600 (labkit top track #16: u and K both membrane-like at t=372; aggregate K rim/core 6.97, rim/outside 1.96). A multilamellar K-free vesicle beside it shrinks from t~51 to ~t=300 and then persists as a small onion to t=600. This is the finding's pattern: the K layer on a closed bilayer survives the resolution change, and persistence is not specific to carrying the catalyst.

observations.B: rerun/seed8/FACTS.md: catalyst K membrane-like (rim/core 6.97, rim/outside 1.96), track #16 u and K membrane-like at t=372; sheet t=132-600: K-ringed double vesicle persists, K-free onion persists beside it

seeds_run.result: K-ringed vesicle at 1.5x persists; K-free vesicle also persists

verdicts.limitation: One seed; 17 of 22 labkit radial members are rings centred on their own hole, so the aggregate radial numbers are rough. Amphiphile totals were not compared with the base grid.
